proposals.before: He gave battle, shattered Fu Deng, and left two-thirds of the enemy dying of thirst; that night Fu Deng's army melted away and he fled to Yong.
proposals.after: He gave battle, shattered Fu Deng, and left two or three tenths of the enemy dying of thirst; that night Fu Deng's army melted away and he fled to Yong.
proposals.reason: Chinese 十二三 means two or three parts in ten, not two-thirds.

proposals.before: Fu Deng had left Fu Guang at Yong and crown prince Fu Chong at Hu Kong; both bolted when they heard of his defeat.
proposals.after: Fu Deng had left Fu Guang at Yong and his son Fu Chong at Hu Kong; both bolted when they heard of his defeat.
proposals.reason: Chinese 子崇 is his son Chong and does not call Fu Chong crown prince.

proposals.before: He made Yao Xu prince of Jin, Yao Shuode prince of Longxi, and ennobled Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and other generals as dukes or marquises.
proposals.after: He made Yao Xu prince of Jin, Yao Shuode prince of Longxi, and ennobled Jing together with meritorious subjects Yin Wei, Qi Nan, Yang Fosong, and others as dukes or marquises.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops 征南靖, omitting the named general Jing present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: He posthumously titled his stepmother Sun empress dowager and enshrined her with the ancestors.
proposals.after: He posthumously titled his concubine-mother Lady Sun empress dowager and enshrined her with the ancestors.
proposals.reason: 庶母 is a father's concubine (Xing's concubine-mother), not necessarily a stepmother.

proposals.before: Fu Deng still lives; civil war would repeat the Yuan brothers' folly and hand victory away.
proposals.after: Fu Deng still lives; civil war would repeat the folly of the two Yuans and hand victory away.
proposals.reason: 二袁 means the two Yuans and does not state that Yuan Shao and Yuan Shu were brothers.

proposals.before: He summoned Ru to be Director of the Secretariat.
proposals.after: He summoned Ru to be a minister of the Secretariat.
proposals.reason: 尚書 here is a Secretariat post, not 尚書令; Director of the Secretariat over-translates the office.

proposals.before: When Murong Yong fell, Liu Gong of Hedong and others held out until Yao Xing sent Yao Xu.
proposals.after: After Murong Yong had been destroyed by Murong Chui, Liu Gong of Hedong and others held out until Yao Xing sent Yao Xu.
proposals.reason: The Chinese names Murong Chui as the destroyer of Murong Yong; the idiomatic sentence omits that agent.

proposals.before: Xue Qiang held Yang's redoubt and guided Yao Xu across at Longmen into Puyang.
proposals.after: Xue Qiang held Yang's redoubt and guided Yao Xu across at Longmen into Puban.
proposals.reason: 蒲阪 is Puban, not Puyang; the following unit renders the same place as Puban.

proposals.before: The General Who Guards the East Xue Qiang first held Yang's fort, led Xu from Longmen to cross the river, and thereupon entered Puyang.
proposals.after: The General Who Guards the East Xue Qiang first held Yang's fort, led Xu from Longmen to cross the river, and thereupon entered Puban.
proposals.reason: 蒲阪 is Puban; Puyang is a different toponym.

proposals.before: Xue Bo fled beyond the passes; Hu of Shang and Ercheng joined him and besieged Yao Xiang at Jincheng.
proposals.after: Xue Bo fled beyond the passes; Hu of Shang commandery and Erchuan joined him and besieged Yao Xiang at Jincheng.
proposals.reason: 貳川 is Erchuan, not Ercheng.

proposals.before: Yao Chong failed at Jinyong against Xiahou Zongzhi but sacked Baigu and deported twenty thousand refugee families.
proposals.after: Yao Chong failed at Jinyong against Xiahou Zongzhi but sacked Baigu and moved more than twenty thousand refugee households of Xihe Yan Yan, Hedong Pei Qi, Han Xi, and others, then returned.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic sentence drops the named refugee leaders 嚴彥、裴岐、韓襲.

proposals.before: Elder scholars such as Jiang Kan, Chunyu Qi, and Gao Guo taught thousands of students in Chang'an.
proposals.after: Elder scholars such as Jiang Kan, Chunyu Qi, and Guo Gao taught in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.
proposals.reason: English reverses the surname-given order of 郭高 as Gao Guo, and 'thousands' understates 萬數千.

proposals.before: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Gao Guo of Fengyi, and others were all aged Confucians of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, each with several hundred disciples, teaching in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.
proposals.after: Jiang Kan of Tianshui, Chunyu Qi of Dongping, Guo Gao of Fengyi, and others were all aged Confucians of great virtue, clear in the classics and cultivated in conduct, each with several hundred disciples, teaching in Chang'an; students who came from afar numbered in the tens of thousands.
proposals.reason: 郭高 is Guo Gao, not Gao Guo.

proposals.before: Hu Bian of Liangzhou had fled to Luoyang with a thousand pupils; Guanzhong students flocked to him.
proposals.after: Hu Bian of Liangzhou, at the end of Fu Jian's time, moved east to Luoyang and lectured to more than a thousand disciples; many later students of Guanzhong went to him to seek instruction.
proposals.reason: 東徙 is eastward relocation, not necessarily flight, and the idiomatic line drops the Fu Jian date.

proposals.before: Gucheng Shen, Wang Shang, Ma Dai, and others of polished prose joined the privy council.
proposals.after: Gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Gucheng Shen, gentleman attendant of the palace secretariat Wang Shang, gentleman of the secretariat Ma Dai, and others, because their compositions were elegant and correct, took part in managing confidential affairs.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line omits the three offices and renders 中書侍郎 too loosely.

proposals.before: Gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Gucheng Shen, palace attendant Wang Shang, gentleman of the secretariat Ma Dai, and others, because their literary compositions were elegant and correct, participated in managing secret matters.
proposals.after: Gentleman attendant at the yellow gate Gucheng Shen, gentleman attendant of the palace secretariat Wang Shang, gentleman of the secretariat Ma Dai, and others, because their literary compositions were elegant and correct, participated in managing secret matters.
proposals.reason: 中書侍郎 is not a generic palace attendant.

proposals.before: Yao Xing rewrote the code along Sun Wu's lines.
proposals.after: Yao Xing read it and deemed it good, then adjusted the code by the oath-taking methods of Sun Wu and Wu Qi.
proposals.reason: 孫吳 names the paired military authorities Sun and Wu, not Sun Wu alone.

proposals.before: Xing read it and deemed it good; thereupon he followed Sun Wu's method of swearing in the host to adjust it.
proposals.after: Xing read it and deemed it good; thereupon he followed the Sun-Wu method of swearing in the host to adjust it.
proposals.reason: 孫吳 is the Sun-Wu pair, not a single person named Sun Wu.

proposals.before: Fearing flatterers would taint his powerful uncles, he gave them honest advisers.
proposals.after: Xu and Shuode's power grew daily; Xing feared crafty petty men would obstruct and bewilder them, and selected pure upright gentlemen to assist them.
proposals.reason: The Chinese does not call them uncles; that kinship is an English interpolation.

proposals.before: Yao Xian urged him to stay home and delegate."
proposals.after: Colonel Director of Retainers Yao Xian came forward and said the emperor was the realm's bulwark and should not campaign in person, but should send the generals with court-approved strategy.
proposals.reason: The idiomatic line is truncated and ends with a stray quote, omitting the speech.

proposals.before: Moyuyu held Shanggui, Lian Quan Luoyang, while Yao Xian and Yao Huang aided the heir in the west palace.
proposals.after: He ordered Moyuyu to provisionally garrison Shanggui, the Central Army commander and Duke of Guangling Lian to garrison Luoyang, and Yao Xian and Director of the Secretariat Yao Huang to assist crown prince Hong on duty in the west palace.
proposals.reason: English fuses 權鎮 (provisionally garrison) into a false name Lian Quan and drops offices.

proposals.before: Yao Xing stopped cold at Puyang.
proposals.after: Yao Xing reached Puban, feared, and did not advance.
proposals.reason: 蒲阪 is Puban, not Puyang (濮陽).

proposals.before: Xing reached Puyang, feared, and did not advance.
proposals.after: Xing reached Puban, feared, and did not advance.
proposals.reason: 蒲阪 is Puban, not Puyang (濮陽).

proposals.before: Shuo De's military orders were orderly; not the slightest hair was violated; he sacrificed to former worthies and honored Confucian sages; the western lands rejoiced in him.
proposals.after: Shuode's military orders were orderly; not the slightest hair was violated; he sacrificed to former worthies and honored Confucian sages; the western lands rejoiced in him.
proposals.reason: The name 碩德 is split as Shuo De rather than Shuode.

proposals.before: He enriched pensions for the Wei dead.
proposals.after: Xing issued a decree generously honoring soldiers who had fallen in battle.
proposals.reason: 軍士戰沒者 are Xing's fallen troops, not the Wei dead.

proposals.before: Wei struck Puyang but Yao Xu's defense drove them off.
proposals.after: Wei advanced on Puban; Yao Xu held firm without giving battle, and Wei withdrew.
proposals.reason: 蒲阪 is Puban, not Puyang (濮陽).

proposals.before: The Wei army exploited victory to advance and attack Puyang; Yao Xu stubbornly defended and did not fight; Wei thereupon led away.
proposals.after: The Wei army exploited victory to advance and attack Puban; Yao Xu stubbornly defended and did not fight; Wei thereupon led away.
proposals.reason: 蒲阪 is Puban, not Puyang (濮陽).

proposals.before: Du Ting of Jingzhao, because Vice Director Qi Nan brought no benefit of support and correction, composed the poem 'Luxuriant Grass' to admonish him; Xiang Yun of Fengyi wrote the rite 'Virtue and the Hunt' to satirize him.
proposals.after: Du Ting of Jingzhao, because Vice Director Qi Nan brought no benefit of support and correction, composed the poem 'Luxuriant Grass' to admonish him; Xiang Yun of Fengyi wrote the rhapsody 'Virtue and the Hunt' to satirize him.
proposals.reason: 德獵賦 is a fu (rhapsody), not a rite.

proposals.before: Peng Quan defected; Yang Fosong took Nanxiang and raided to Liang.
proposals.after: Jin's Administrator of Shunyang Peng Quan surrendered his commandery to Xing; Xing sent Yang Fosong with five thousand cavalry and his Inspector of Jingzhou Zhao Yao to receive him; they then took Nanxiang, captured General Who Establishes Might Liu Song, raided as far as Liang, and returned.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits Zhao Yao, Liu Song, Xing's order, and the five thousand cavalry present in the Chinese.

proposals.before: Earlier Xin Gongjing had refused to bow; Yao Xing had offered him office."
proposals.after: Earlier Xin Gongjing had refused to bow; Yao Xing had offered him office.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quotation mark with no matching opener.

proposals.before: Xing with Roshi and the śramaṇas Seng Lüe, Seng Qian, Dao Shu, Seng Rui, Dao Tan, Seng Zhao, Tan Shun, and more than eight hundred others newly produced the Great Perfection of Wisdom; Rosi held the Hu text, Xing held the old translation, and they collated them; wherever the new text differed from the old, all accorded with principle and meaning.
proposals.after: Xing with Roshi and the śramaṇas Seng Lüe, Seng Qian, Dao Shu, Seng Rui, Dao Tan, Seng Zhao, Tan Shun, and more than eight hundred others newly produced the Great Perfection of Wisdom; Roshi held the Hu text, Xing held the old translation, and they collated them; wherever the new text differed from the old, all accorded with principle and meaning.
proposals.reason: Literal English misspells 羅什 as Rosi after already using Roshi in the same sentence.

proposals.before: Tufa Nutan sent three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
proposals.after: Tufa Nutan presented Yao Xing three thousand horses and thirty thousand sheep.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English drops the explicit recipient 興 (Xing) present in the Chinese and the literal line.

proposals.before: Two hundred Liangzhou notables begged to keep Wang Shang; Yao Xing refused.
proposals.after: More than two hundred men of Liangzhou, including Shentu Ying, sent chief clerk Hu Wei to Yao Xing, begging to retain Wang Shang; Xing refused.
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English omits the named petitioners 申屠英 and envoy 胡威, collapsing them into unnamed notables.

proposals.before: In the past Han Wu tilted the realm's resources to open Hexi, cut off the various Rong, severed the Xiongnu' right arm—therefore in the end he could slaughter the King of Dayuan, Wu Guan.
proposals.after: In the past Han Wu tilted the realm's resources to open Hexi, cut off the various Rong, severed the Xiongnu's right arm—therefore in the end he could slaughter the King of Dayuan, Wugua.
proposals.reason: 毋寡 is Wugua, the King of Dayuan; Wu Guan is a wrong transcription, and the Xiongnu possessive is broken.

proposals.before: How He Dingyuan alone was lofty, Ying Ping alone beautiful!
proposals.after: How could Dingyuan alone be lofty, or Yingping alone beautiful!
proposals.reason: 何 is rhetorical how, not surname He; 定遠 and 營平 are the marquisate titles of Ban Chao and Zhao Chongguo.

proposals.before: What need of famous generals of old?
proposals.after: How could Dingyuan alone be lofty, or Yingping alone beautiful!
proposals.reason: Idiomatic English erases the two named historical exemplars 定遠 and 營平.

proposals.before: Yao Xing asked Yao Wenzu about Zong Chang."
proposals.after: Yao Xing asked Yao Wenzu about Zong Chang.
proposals.reason: Stray closing quote with no opening quote; the Chinese also says Xing read the memorial and was greatly pleased.
